title: land merges a rebase conflict confined to one-line kb/_self doc hunks that two items edited at different words, so a sibling's doc row edit does not stop it at step rebase
goal: when the rebase of land stops only on kb/_self/*.md lines that both sides changed at different words (a table row or a one-line paragraph), land merges the line word by word keeping both sides, continues the rebase and says which lines it merged; a conflict on the same words, or in any other file, still stops it at step rebase

run:
import sys;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import bl_land as l
f=getattr(l,"merge_line_hunks",None)
b="| a | imports x and y, never z |";o="| a | imports x, y and w, never z |";t="| a | imports x and y, never z (always q) |"
r=f(b,o,t) if f else None;same=f(b,"| a | imports k |","| a | imports m |") if f else "x"
print("merged:",r,"| same-words conflict refused:",same is None)
sys.exit(0 if r=="| a | imports x, y and w, never z (always q) |" and same is None else 1)

notes: SP-z3hyk4eh retrospective: three of nine landings stopped at step rebase (backlog.py ops: ST-zqbo7xgc 13:26, BG-wqc6sgug 13:30, ST-6tz7yhem 13:45, each land.step rebase exit=1): siblings edited different words of the same one-line rows of kb/_self/tools.md, backlog.md and code.md, which the rules treat as no overlap (backlog.md, Running a sprint: a shared doc orders no two items). The orchestrator resolved each by a word-level merge keeping both sides, by hand. The function name in the check is a proposal; the planner may rename it with the check.
